relationships.description: The application function reads, creates or modifies the state held in the data object while it performs its work, treating the data structure as passive material.
relationships.evidence: The function's implementing methods instantiate, read fields of, or mutate the class, record or struct that defines the data object, for example by taking it as a parameter or returning it.

relationships.description: The application function performs operations on the protected resource and is therefore a subject whose actions fall under that resource's access-control rules.
relationships.evidence: The function's code invokes an operation on the resource that the security policy names, such as a repository call on a guarded entity, or carries the permission check or annotation that the resource definition declares.

relationships.description: The application function contributes a capability that the application process relies on to reach its defined end result, so the function's output is part of what makes the process worthwhile.
relationships.evidence: A step in the workflow, saga or orchestration method calls the function's entry point, and design documentation credits the function with producing part of the process outcome.

relationships.description: The application function supplies the internal capability whose results give the externally offered application service its usefulness to consumers.
relationships.evidence: The service's operation handlers delegate to the function's methods, and service documentation names the function as the source of the behavior the service offers.

relationships.description: The application function cannot carry out its work unless the application event occurs, because it reacts to that event or needs the state change the event signals.
relationships.evidence: The function is registered as a listener, subscriber or handler for the event type, through a decorator, a message-consumer binding or an event-bus subscription.

relationships.description: The source application function needs the capability of another internal application function in order to complete its own work.
relationships.evidence: The source function's implementation imports and calls the other function's methods, or receives it as an injected collaborator.

relationships.description: The application function requires the data object's structure to be available and stable, so that changes to the data structure break or alter the function.
relationships.evidence: The function's signatures, imports or type annotations reference the data object's class or type, so the function fails to compile or run without it.

relationships.description: Data or control produced by the source application function is handed on to the target application function, which continues the processing.
relationships.evidence: The source function's return value or emitted payload is passed directly into the target function, through a call chain, a pipeline wiring or a queue that connects the two.

relationships.description: The application function is the internal behavior that concretely implements the operations the application service exposes to its consumers.
relationships.evidence: The service interface or API contract is implemented by classes or methods belonging to the function, for example a service implementation class that contains the function's logic.

relationships.description: The application function automates the competency described by the business function, so that software carries out work the business function groups.
relationships.evidence: Architecture or capability-mapping documentation maps the application module to the business function, and the module's logic implements that business area's rules, such as payroll calculation for HR management.

relationships.description: The application function's behavior meets the stated need, so the requirement is fulfilled by what the function does.
relationships.evidence: A requirements-traceability matrix, ticket link or code annotation ties the function's implementation to the requirement ID, and acceptance tests for the requirement exercise the function.

notes: delivers-value to ApplicationService largely duplicates realizes ApplicationService. depends-on DataObject overlaps accesses DataObject. delivers-value is a traceability predicate meant for business value, so applying it to ApplicationProcess is questionable; consumed-by or serves would fit better.
